name: SeaQuest
notes: No official SeaQuest/E906 Fermilab website was found (DNS failures and refused connections on several tried subdomains); the record relies on INSPIRE, the spectrometer arXiv paper, the December 2025 final-results arXiv paper, and a U.S. DOE categorical-exclusion record (CX-002672) for the NM4 hall name and project goals.
Exact data-taking start/end calendar years were not confirmed by any source consulted and are therefore not asserted (see the 'completed' interval note).

physics_goals.locator: title (flavor asymmetry via Drell-Yan); nuclear-modification goal in DOE CX-002672
physics_goals.note: The d-bar/u-bar flavor asymmetry via Drell-Yan is the subject of the collaboration's final-results paper; the nuclear-modification goal is from the 2010 DOE determination: 'the modifications to that structure which occur when the nucleon is embedded in a nucleus'.
physics_goals.quote: Final SeaQuest results on the flavor asymmetry of the proton light-quark sea with proton-induced Drell-Yan process
physics_goals.value: Measure the antiquark flavor asymmetry (d̄/ū) in the proton sea via the Drell-Yan process, and study how nuclear binding modifies the quark/antiquark structure of nucleons

summary.plain: SeaQuest was a Fermilab experiment that fired a proton beam at hydrogen and deuterium targets to measure how down and up antiquarks are distributed differently inside a proton, finishing its analysis in 2025.
summary.technical: Fixed-target Drell-Yan dimuon experiment (Fermilab E-906) in the NM4 hall, using a 120 GeV proton beam (Main Injector) on liquid-hydrogen, liquid-deuterium and solid nuclear targets to measure the proton's d̄/ū sea-quark flavor asymmetry and nuclear modification effects; its final combined-data-set results were posted in December 2025.
